judgments.reasoning_cat1: A demanding compliance condition softened by a proviso that it "may be satisfied by Fund providing to Lender such reasonable assurances as Lender may require" — the proviso largely undoes the condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps 5.3, which represents that all aspects of Borrowers' operations and the Offering Circular comply with applicable law; the condition and the representation are not calibrated the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated diligence list with a subjective satisfaction standard; conventional for a closing condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(j) and (s); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific financial statements identified by period; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.11's representation about the latest financial statements delivered before the Closing Date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed eight-item delivery list tied to a $250,000,000 threshold; several items are qualified "if available", which weakens the requirement in an unspecified way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The list differs in content and order from the near-identical list in the Eligible Notes Receivable definition clause (r) (c063), and 3.3(e) and 4.2 repeat the $250,000,000 test; keeping the three aligned is a genuine problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure sweep-up condition ("all other documents and legal matters ... satisfactory to Lender") appended to a long list of specifics — the classic general-after-specific formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits at the end of 3.1's enumerated conditions and would, read broadly, swallow them; the funding-as-waiver rule in 3.1's opener mitigates this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is mis-numbered "4.2" in the text although the section is 3.2, and a single condition subsequent ("a hired a full time Controller") contains a stray word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Making failure of a condition subsequent an automatic Event of Default interacts with Section 8's default list and 3.3's conditions precedent; the numbering slip could confuse cross-references.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "true and correct in all material respects" with an earlier-date carve-out; standard and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Section 5 introduction (c262), which uses the same bring-down formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; the omitted final punctuation is immaterial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Default and Event of Default definitions and Section 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific and objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four words resting entirely on the vague "Material Adverse Change" standard, with no time reference for measuring the change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Material Adverse Change definition (c112) supplies content, and 5.11 fixes a baseline date for the representation, but this condition itself specifies no baseline.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender" qualifies an otherwise numeric test; the sentence also ends mid-thought with "and".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates 3.1(t) and 4.2's $250,000,000 possession requirement; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "a current Borrowing Base Certificate" — "current" is undefined, though 6.2(b) sets delivery timing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 6.2(b), which requires a Borrowing Base calculation on the date of each Advance, the requirement is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed three-year term with an immediate termination right on an Event of Default, qualified by "subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided"; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 3.6 Effect of Termination and 3.7's prepayment premium, which contemplate termination before the Maturity Date; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is labelled 3.5 but reads "3.4 Intentionally Blank", duplicating the number of the preceding Term section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.4 is the operative Term provision, so the mis-numbering creates a superficial clash with c243, though nothing turns on a blank section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and internally consistent; the cash-collateral parenthetical gives Lender an unqualified determination right but says so expressly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 3.7 and 2.3(b)(F)-(G)'s cash collateral mechanics; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear notice period and payment mechanics; the repeated cash-collateral parenthetical is verbose but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with the Applicable Prepayment Premium definition (c011) and 3.7(b); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A liquidated-damages style premium payable on any early termination "for any reason not set forth in Section 3.7(a)", including foreclosure and plan confirmation, closed by the word "if applicable" — which leaves it unclear when the premium is in fact due.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The premium falls to zero after the first anniversary under c011, so much of the enumerated list is inoperative; the cross-reference in the text is also garbled ("Section 3.'Mfa)").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean grant of security interest; the final sentence flatly bars disposition of "any item or portion of the Collateral" except Permitted Dispositions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That bar must be reconciled with 4.9(b)'s release-on-sale mechanic, 2.6(a)(iii)'s treatment of sale proceeds and 7.4; whether an unauthorised sale is void or merely a breach is a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains an embedded allonge form and a $250,000,000 possession threshold; detailed but with "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender" left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The requirement to hold only $250,000,000 of notes while the Borrowing Base counts all Eligible Notes Receivable leaves a gap between what Lender holds and what it lends against — a real tension with c035 and c063(r)/(s).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Remedies are clearly conditioned on an Event of Default, and the trust obligation for Collections is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.6(a)'s deposit obligation and 4.8's servicing rights; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any financing statement necessary or desirable" is broad but is the standard Article 9 authorisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(a), the Filing Authorization Letter (c076) and 4.4(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific three-Business-Day deadline and a defined deliverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.7(d)'s representation and Borrower Collateral (c032)(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An open-ended obligation to deliver "all other documents ... that Lender may request in its Permitted Discretion", plus detailed IP registration mechanics that sit oddly in a mortgage-fund facility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The copyright/patent machinery has little to work on given 5.16 and the nature of the business, and the Real Property mortgage obligation here goes beyond Borrower Collateral (c032), which does not enumerate Real Property.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear assignment of access rights conditioned on an Event of Default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 5.5's public-warehouse proviso, which contemplates assigned access; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated power of attorney; clauses (a), (c) and (d) are exercisable without any default, which is broader than the rest and could be argued to be inconsistent with the clause's protective purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unconditional endorsement power in (d) sits alongside 4.3, which conditions collection on an Event of Default; the difference is deliberate but noticeable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad inspection rights qualified by "reasonable notice" and "normal business hours"; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1, 6.2 and 6.5(c)'s appraisal-discussion rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any or all reasonable steps" is loose phrasing, but the Code sections identified give it content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Control Agreement definition (c053) and 2.6(d); note the liquidation right here is triggered by a mere Default, whereas 4.3 requires an Event of Default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants Borrowers discretion to take "such action with respect to the Notes Receivable as the Borrowers may deem advisable" — a broad subjective standard sitting inside an otherwise controlled servicing regime.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The revocation right is exercisable "in accordance with the terms of the Servicing Agreement", a document not before the reader, and 4.3 gives Lender a parallel right to install a replacement servicer; the two need reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear trigger (repayment in entirety) and clear obligation; the requirement to return the note "to facilitate its payment" after it is already repaid is slightly circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 4.9(b) and (c); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When a Note Receivable is sold by Fund in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, Lender shall release the Lender's Liens" makes the release turn on the wholly unspecified phrase "in accordance with the terms of this Agreement", and "against payment of the agreed amount therefor" leaves it unclear who fixes the agreed amount and whether payment is a condition of release.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with Permitted Dispositions (c127)(e), which requires a cash price of at least 80% of the unpaid balance paid directly to a Cash Management Account, with 2.6(a)(iii)'s direct-payment requirement and with 4.1's flat prohibition on disposing of Collateral — whether a sale outside those terms nonetheless releases the Lien is a genuine internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated triggers with a defined deliverable; "reasonably acceptable to Lender" is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Trigger (ii) uses the same undefined "in accordance with the terms of this Agreement" formula as 4.9(b) (c260), so it inherits that provision's uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard bring-down language with a materiality qualifier and an earlier-date carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 3.3(a) (c237); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "good and indefeasible title" is a term of art of contested content, and it is used for personal property while "good and marketable title" is used for Real Property.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.2 and the Permitted Liens definition; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (i) requires the note to be secured by real property "on which a commercial or residential development is located or is expected to be built" — "expected" by whom, and on what basis, is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (i) also conflicts in emphasis with Eligible Notes Receivable clause (a) (c063), which requires a commercial loan for purchasing commercial or residential real estate, and with the Note Receivable definition (c119) requiring maker-owned property.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "commensurate with forms and documentation used by prudent lenders in the same or similar circumstances" is a vague external benchmark, and the flat representation that everything complies with all applicable laws is unqualified by materiality in its second half.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Eligible Notes Receivable clause (g) (c063) and 3.1(m)/(p)'s approval of the same forms; the unqualified compliance representation about the Offering Circular is broader than 3.1(q)'s conditional formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "fit for such purposes" is a short, soft representation, but the subject matter is trivial in this facility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Equipment definition (c069) and 6.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso permitting storage of loan files in "a public warehouse, access to which has been assigned by a Borrower to Lender" is an exception whose scope (which files, which warehouses) is loosely drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the flat statement in the same sentence that Collateral "is not stored with a bailee, warehouseman, or similar party", and 6.9 requires a Collateral Access Agreement for new locations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, plain representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1's accounting system covenant and the Books definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule-referential; the schedule number is OCR-garbled ("3.7(a)") but recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.9 and the Code's perfection rules; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule-referential and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.9, which permits amendment of Schedule 5.7(b) on 30 days' notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule-referential and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as of a fixed date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4(b)'s obligation for after-acquired commercial tort claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing parenthetical "(as may be necessary by the applicable laws of such state)" is garbled and redundant of the preceding clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(e)-(f) and 6.12; no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Other than as described on Schedule 5.8 or in an Offering Circular" makes an unattached, changeable document a carve-out from the representation, leaving its scope indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Offering Circular definition (c122) is itself a collective, amendable bundle, so the carve-out could expand over time against 5.20's fixed Closing Date snapshot.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses corporate share vocabulary for LLC subsidiaries but the meaning is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subsidiary definition (c155) excludes several entities, so a "complete and accurate list" of Subsidiaries may exclude affiliated funds — coherent but easily misread.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same Offering Circular carve-out as 5.8(b), applied to Subsidiaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same interaction with c122 and the narrowed Subsidiary definition; consistent in structure with 5.8(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line authorisation representation; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.1(c)'s resolutions certificate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "material contractual obligation" is undefined, but the clause is otherwise a conventional no-conflict representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iii)'s carve-out for Permitted Liens aligns with 7.2 and 5.9(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against 3.1(q), which contemplates that licences and approvals may be required for the Investor Membership Interest offering; the two are not obviously aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy/equity exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16.4 Severability; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States the Liens are "validly created, perfected, and first priority" as of the representation date, which is a legal conclusion rather than a fact but is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "subject only to Permitted Liens" is in tension with the assertion of first priority, since Permitted Liens (c130) includes categories that would rank ahead; 2.1(b)(ii) expressly contemplates superior-priority Liens.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A triple-nested set of exclusions ("other than ... and other than ... and other than") makes the sentence hard to parse, and "reasonably could not be expected to result in a Material Adverse Change" inverts the usual formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in substance with 6.3(g)'s litigation notice requirement, which uses the more usual "reasonably could be expected" phrasing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear baseline ("since the date of the latest financial statements submitted to Lender on or before the Closing Date") and standard GAAP carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplies the baseline that 3.3(d) (c240) lacks; the two provisions therefore need to be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-word representation resting entirely on the defined term "Solvent".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Solvent definition (c150) uses only a balance-sheet test, which does not match the fraudulent-transfer concepts invoked by the heading of Section 5.12 and by 5.12(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the statutory actual-intent language; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with 5.12(a) and the Solvent definition; the section addresses intent but not constructive fraudulent transfer, a gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat negative representation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Benefit Plan and ERISA Affiliate definitions; no covenant elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge-qualified in (a) and (b) but not in (c) and (d), an asymmetry that could matter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.13's environmental covenants and the Environmental Lien definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An absolute representation extending to fees payable "by Borrowers or any other Person", which no Borrower could reliably know.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No indemnity or covenant elsewhere addresses broker fees, so the representation stands alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard IP representation with a schedule; the singular "its business" against plural Borrowers is a minor slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4(c)'s IP registration covenants, though those covenants are more elaborate than this business requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "peaceful and undisturbed possession" and "material to their business" are soft but conventional lease representations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.11's covenant to pay rent and the Permitted Protest carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule-based listing requirement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.7 Control Agreements and 2.6; "as updated from time to time" is unaccompanied by any update mechanic, unlike 6.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "taken as a whole" appears three times and materially changes what the representation covers; a court would have to decide what unit of information is being tested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with 6.14 Disclosure Updates, which requires correction of untrue statements but expressly says notification does not cure the earlier breach; the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such detail ... as is satisfactory to Lender" makes the adequacy of the schedule a matter of Lender's judgment inside a representation of truth and completeness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.20 is also the list of permitted Indebtedness under 7.1(b), so its content has covenant consequences; consistent in structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward schedule representation with an anti-affiliate condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Approved Title Insurance Company definition (c013), which allows Lender to add or remove companies, and with the Affiliate definition (c008)'s special 10% rule.
